excluded_types.business-domain: Implementation, tests, drift, and proof evidence are part of the requested graph.
excluded_types.system-runtime: The business promise and formal clause must remain the meaning owners.
excluded_types.architecture-property: The primary job is intent-to-implementation traceability, not structural enforcement alone.

purpose: Represent the Financial Settlement P4 path as typed business, bridge, and system nodes so the UI projects an ontology graph instead of treating a Markdown anchor as the ontology.
boundary: This ontology is a candidate-local evidence read model. It does not mutate DomainSpec meaning, manufacture missing concept bindings, generate TypeScript, issue a proof receipt, or grant promotion authority.

branches.role: Owns domain meaning and desired behavior.
Owns traceability, evidence gaps, drift, and proof-state explanations.
Records implementation and test artifacts without redefining business meaning.

node_contract.forbidden_collapse: A source file is evidence for a node, not the node itself. Matching names or prose anchors do not create cross-branch identity.

nodes.label: Pay the player once
nodes.plain_language: When a player is eligible, the organization pays that settlement exactly once and records that payment.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This is the human outcome that every clause, proof concern, architecture contract, implementation, and receipt must preserve.

properties.promise_scope: eligibility, one payout, and one durable payment record

nodes.claim_ceiling: A plain-language synthesis of the current semantic graph; not a newly promoted canonical definition or a proof that payment happens.

nodes.label: Work out the payout amount
nodes.plain_language: Calculate the player share that supplies the settlement amount.
nodes.claim_ceiling: A generated semantic node; not implementation evidence.

nodes.label: Complete the settlement
nodes.plain_language: Perform the business action that writes an eligible payout and records that it happened.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: Reason outward from this business action: every obligation, architecture shape, and implementation candidate must preserve what completing settlement means.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Operation meaning only; no implementation identity is asserted.

nodes.label: Remember that payment happened
nodes.plain_language: Record the business fact that the payout was created.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Event meaning only; not evidence that runtime emission occurred.

nodes.label: Decide whether payment is allowed
nodes.plain_language: Allow a positive payout only when an equivalent payout does not already exist.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Rule meaning only; no code binding is asserted.

nodes.label: Pay once and record it
nodes.plain_language: When a positive payout is due and none exists, write one PAYOUT and then emit one PayoutCreated event.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: Use this clause as the behavioral yardstick: a payout write without the following event is an incomplete settlement.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Candidate formal meaning; not an executable proof.

nodes.label: DomainSpec semantic graph
nodes.plain_language: The DomainSpec read model gives stable identities and typed relationships to the Financial Settlement business concepts and P4 clause.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: Use this graph to preserve stable identities and relationships before deriving checks or comparing the business meaning with code.
nodes.claim_ceiling: A DomainSpec semantic projection; it does not prove the system or replace authored business authority.

nodes.label: DomainSpec Operation
nodes.plain_language: The DomainSpec type for a business action that changes system state.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: Because this concept is an Operation, look for a state-changing realization rather than treating it as a value calculation or yes-or-no rule.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Projection of the active meta-type; this ontology does not admit or promote it.

nodes.label: DomainSpec Calculation
nodes.plain_language: The DomainSpec type for a deterministic pure function that returns a value.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Projection of the active meta-type; no architecture realization type is currently mapped.

nodes.label: DomainSpec Rule
nodes.plain_language: The DomainSpec type for a boolean guard that blocks or allows behavior.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Projection of the active meta-type; this ontology does not bind it to the handwritten decision function.

nodes.label: DomainSpec Event
nodes.plain_language: The DomainSpec type for a typed fact describing something that already happened.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Projection of the active meta-type; no architecture realization type is currently mapped.

nodes.label: DomainSpec test derivation
nodes.plain_language: The DomainSpec test-derivation artifacts assign stable obligation identities and describe what can or cannot be executed.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This model translates formal meaning into named checks, but deriving a check does not prove that the behavior passed.
nodes.claim_ceiling: It contains derived obligations but does not establish the missing P4 subject identity.

nodes.label: Operation implementation shape
nodes.plain_language: A candidate architecture type describing how a DomainSpec Operation may be represented in code.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This candidate shape narrows what compliant code should look like while deliberately stopping before it chooses a specific function.
nodes.claim_ceiling: A candidate type alignment, not a binding to any source function.

nodes.label: Rule implementation shape
nodes.plain_language: A candidate TypeScript shape for a DomainSpec Rule: one bound boolean callable in the rule folder, using the configured source and export conventions.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This type turns the abstract Rule classification into constraints a TypeScript evaluator can inspect without pretending a folder creates business meaning.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Candidate profile constraints only; the current settlement decision function has not been adapted and evaluated as this type.

nodes.label: Only eligible payouts pass
nodes.plain_language: Show that a payout is allowed only when the settlement eligibility rule is true.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This concern isolates the decision boundary so a passing settlement path cannot hide an eligibility failure.
nodes.claim_ceiling: The current checks cover selected rule cases; they do not prove the complete settlement promise.

nodes.label: The same settlement ID pays once
nodes.plain_language: Send the same settlement identity again and show that a second payout is not created.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This concern gives the phrase never twice a concrete identity-based attack that the proof plan must defeat.

properties.evidence_posture: generated and handwritten duplicate checks exist
properties.question: Can the same identity produce two payouts?

nodes.claim_ceiling: Existing duplicate checks are not bound into the complete P4 receipt and do not cover concurrent requests.

nodes.label: Simultaneous requests still pay once
nodes.plain_language: Race multiple requests for the same settlement and show that only one can create the payout.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This concern prevents a sequential duplicate test from being mistaken for evidence about races between simultaneous requests.

properties.question: Can two requests pass the duplicate check at the same time?

nodes.claim_ceiling: A planned concern with no current concurrency execution evidence.

nodes.label: One payout produces one payment record
nodes.plain_language: Show that a created payout emits exactly one PayoutCreated event, rather than zero or multiple events.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This concern keeps the durable record promise separate from payout creation because the current optional handler can break that connection.

properties.evidence_posture: positive test exists but handler is optional
properties.question: Does every created payout leave exactly one event?

nodes.claim_ceiling: The positive test does not establish event delivery in every configuration.

nodes.label: Write before announcing payment
nodes.plain_language: Observe that the payout write completes before PayoutCreated is emitted.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This concern distinguishes code order from observed effect order so the proof cannot infer runtime behavior from adjacent lines alone.

properties.question: Can the event escape before the payout is durable?

nodes.claim_ceiling: Static source order is visible, but no bound runtime observation proves the effect order.

nodes.label: Retries recover without a second payout
nodes.plain_language: Interrupt or retry settlement execution and show that recovery neither loses the record nor creates another payout.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This concern exposes the failure window between durable state and event delivery instead of assuming retries are automatically safe.

properties.question: What happens after a partial failure and retry?

nodes.claim_ceiling: A planned recovery concern with no current failure-injection evidence.

nodes.label: High request volume preserves the promise
nodes.plain_language: Apply sustained and burst traffic and show that the system still prevents duplicate payouts and records accepted payouts.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This concern prevents functional checks from being stretched into resilience claims that require a different execution environment.

properties.question: Does overload weaken the once-only guarantee?

nodes.claim_ceiling: A planned resilience concern with no current load or capacity evidence.

nodes.label: Prove the payout write and event
nodes.plain_language: Check that the first eligible payout creates the payment record and its event without allowing a duplicate.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: Treat this obligation as the question that evidence must answer; the existence of the question is not evidence of a passing answer.
nodes.claim_ceiling: A derived testing artifact, not a DomainSpec meta-type or passing proof.

nodes.label: Block a duplicate payout
nodes.plain_language: Check that an existing payout prevents another payout decision.
nodes.claim_ceiling: This checks the pure R5 decision, not the full P4 effects.

nodes.label: Allow the first payout
nodes.plain_language: Check that a positive payout with no existing payout is allowed.
nodes.claim_ceiling: This checks the pure R5 decision, not the full P4 effects.

nodes.label: Candidate settlement code contract
nodes.plain_language: A TypeScript Operation realization would receive payout context, decide eligibility, write the payout, and emit the event after the write.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: Use this contract as the comparison target for code inputs and effects without assuming that any current function already satisfies or owns it.
nodes.claim_ceiling: A proposed bridge contract; it neither binds nor generates the existing code.

nodes.label: Candidate eligibility rule code contract
nodes.plain_language: The eligibility decision is modeled as one semantically bound TypeScript boolean arrow function in its own rule file, imported by the Operation through the admitted dependency shape.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This contract ties the Rule meta-type to inspectable source properties while leaving the current handwritten decision function unbound until an adapter supplies observed facts.
nodes.claim_ceiling: A candidate structural contract; no current settlement source adapter or conformance receipt satisfies it yet.

nodes.label: Rule unit checks
nodes.plain_language: Run focused checks for the first allowed payout and the duplicate-block decision.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: These checks answer narrow eligibility questions quickly, but they cannot observe persistence, event delivery, concurrency, recovery, or load behavior.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Executable unit evidence for selected rule obligations, not the complete settlement promise.

nodes.label: Duplicate-ID integration check
nodes.plain_language: Execute the settlement path twice with the same identity and inspect the stored payout count.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This strategy connects the duplicate concern to a real use-case check while preserving the missing P4 obligation binding.
nodes.claim_ceiling: A handwritten sequential check; not bound to FS-POST-001 and not concurrency evidence.

nodes.label: Concurrent duplicate race
nodes.plain_language: Release multiple same-ID settlement requests together and observe that exactly one payout is committed.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This planned strategy exercises the race that sequential idempotency tests cannot reach and therefore must remain a separate evidence class.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Planned strategy only; no concurrency test result or receipt exists.

nodes.label: Payment-event integration check
nodes.plain_language: Create a payout with an event handler and inspect that one PayoutCreated event was emitted.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This strategy observes the event on the positive path but cannot erase the ontology drift caused by the optional handler.
nodes.claim_ceiling: A positive handwritten check; not bound to FS-POST-001 and not evidence for handler-absent behavior.

nodes.label: Missing or early event must fail
nodes.plain_language: Deliberately remove or misorder the event and require the complete P4 checker to reject the run.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This negative control demonstrates that the proof harness notices a broken half of the promise instead of passing on payout creation alone.
nodes.claim_ceiling: The control is modeled but has not been executed in a bound complete-P4 harness.

nodes.label: Failure-and-retry check
nodes.plain_language: Inject failures around payout persistence and event delivery, retry, and inspect payout and event counts.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This planned strategy makes recovery behavior observable instead of treating retry safety as a consequence of ordinary happy-path tests.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Planned strategy only; no recovery or failure-injection result exists.

nodes.label: Settlement load and burst check
nodes.plain_language: Exercise sustained and burst request volumes while measuring accepted payouts, duplicates, failures, and event records.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This planned strategy owns resilience evidence so unit and integration checks are not misrepresented as proof under operational pressure.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Planned strategy only; no capacity threshold, environment, or load result exists.

nodes.label: Architecture conformance evaluation
nodes.plain_language: Adapt source facts into the architecture ontology and evaluate the selected Rule and Operation constraints with positive and negative controls.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This strategy can verify code shape independently from business behavior, while both evidence families remain necessary for a trustworthy receipt.
nodes.claim_ceiling: The evaluator works on observed-fact fixtures; no Poker Team source adapter or settlement conformance receipt exists.

nodes.label: Payout decision function
nodes.plain_language: Handwritten TypeScript allows a positive first payout and blocks an existing payout.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This function supports eligibility reasoning, but it covers only the decision portion of the larger payout-write-and-event promise.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Observed function source; no DomainSpec Rule identity is asserted.

nodes.label: Settlement execution function
nodes.plain_language: Handwritten TypeScript calls the decision function, writes the payout, and conditionally emits PayoutCreated.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This is a plausible execution site, yet similarity of name and behavior cannot establish an ontology binding to GenerateSettlement.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Observed function source; no GenerateSettlement concept binding is asserted.

nodes.label: PAYOUT write site
nodes.plain_language: The use case contains the source location that writes the PAYOUT record.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Static source location; not a runtime occurrence.

nodes.label: PayoutCreated emission site
nodes.plain_language: The use case contains the source location that emits PayoutCreated when an event handler exists.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Static conditional source location; not a runtime occurrence.

nodes.label: Generated P4 test case
nodes.plain_language: The generated test names FS-POST-001 but skips execution because the full behavior is side-effectful.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: A skipped generated test records recognized coverage work, but because it never executes it supplies no proof evidence.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Representation of an obligation, not an executed test.

nodes.label: Generated duplicate-block check
nodes.plain_language: The generated check calls the decision function with an existing payout and expects rejection.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This check supports the duplicate-block decision for its bound rule, not the complete settlement effects required by P4.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Executable pure-decision check only.

nodes.label: Generated first-payout check
nodes.plain_language: The generated check calls the decision function with no existing payout and expects permission.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This check supports permission for the first payout at the decision level, not evidence that the write and event occurred.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Executable pure-decision check only.

nodes.label: Payout write check
nodes.plain_language: A handwritten test observes that the use case requests a PAYOUT write for a positive payout.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This test supplies one persistence observation, but without obligation binding it remains a fragment rather than a complete P4 proof.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Behavior check with no FS-POST-001 identity.

nodes.label: Duplicate payout check
nodes.plain_language: A handwritten test observes that an existing payout prevents another write.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Behavior check with no FS-POST-001 identity.

nodes.label: PayoutCreated check
nodes.plain_language: A handwritten test observes the PayoutCreated payload when an event handler is supplied.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: This test shows that an event can be emitted, but it does not challenge the missing-handler case or prove the complete effect order.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Behavior check with no FS-POST-001 identity and no missing-handler challenge.

nodes.label: Ontology-native obligation origin is missing
nodes.plain_language: FS-POST-001 has a legacy prose anchor but no graph digest, node ID, clause ID, or JSON pointer to P4.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: Because the obligation lacks a native subject reference, matching names must not be used to infer a direct identity with P4.
nodes.claim_ceiling: The ontology must not manufacture a P4-to-obligation edge.

nodes.label: Complete P4 harness binding is missing
nodes.plain_language: No single executable harness binds FS-POST-001 to the payout write, event, duplicate block, and their combined verdict.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: Separate passing tests do not combine into proof unless one harness binds every required observation to the same obligation.
nodes.claim_ceiling: No current test suite proves FS-POST-001.

nodes.label: Write-before-event observation is missing
nodes.plain_language: The code is statically ordered, but no obligation-bound test observes the write before the event.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Static source order is not runtime-order proof.

nodes.label: Operation-to-code binding is missing
nodes.plain_language: The use-case name and behavior resemble GenerateSettlement, but no owner-resolved concept binding establishes identity.
nodes.claim_ceiling: No realized_by or generated_as edge may be asserted yet.

nodes.label: The event is optional in code
nodes.plain_language: P4 requires one PayoutCreated event, while the current source emits it only when an event handler exists.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: Because the code may omit the event, evidence of a payout write alone cannot satisfy the complete P4 promise.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Source-level candidate drift; runtime frequency and production impact are unknown.

nodes.label: Derivation tier and executable coverage disagree
nodes.plain_language: The obligation table classifies P4 as derivable-pure, while the current binding and emitted test classify the full behavior as side-effectful and skipped.
nodes.claim_ceiling: A classification contradiction, not a resolution.

nodes.label: Missing-event negative control
nodes.plain_language: Allow a positive first payout without an event handler and require the complete evaluator to fail.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: A trustworthy evaluator must reject this missing-event case; otherwise it cannot distinguish a complete settlement from an incomplete one.
nodes.claim_ceiling: A planned control, not an executed result.

nodes.label: FS-POST-001 proof receipt
nodes.plain_language: Eventually bind the ontology subject, obligation, exact code and tests, observations, negative control, and verdict.
nodes.reasoning_sentence: Only an issued receipt can combine identities, observations, controls, and verdict into one reviewable proof claim.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Receipt target only; no receipt or passing verdict exists.

nodes.label: Financial Settlement proof-to-code view
nodes.plain_language: Arrange the selected business meaning, DomainSpec formal model, proof bridge, and existing evidence into one explainable view.
nodes.claim_ceiling: An explanatory projection; it does not add authority or evidence to the selected graph.

nodes.label: Business meaning
nodes.plain_language: The business concepts and formal promise that later artifacts must preserve.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Presentation membership only; it does not change business ownership.

nodes.label: DomainSpec formal model
nodes.plain_language: The semantic graph, meta-type classification, and derived obligation model that structure the business meaning.
nodes.claim_ceiling: A read-model lane; it does not redefine DomainSpec authority.

nodes.label: Proof and architecture bridge
nodes.plain_language: The obligations, candidate code shapes, gaps, controls, and receipt target between meaning and system evidence.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Shows supported and missing bridges; it does not manufacture them.

nodes.label: Existing system evidence
nodes.plain_language: The handwritten functions and test artifacts that currently exist in the system.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Groups observed evidence; it does not establish implementation conformance.

nodes.label: Explain these boxes
nodes.plain_language: Guide a reader through the semantic roles, supported relationships, and deliberately missing relationship in the proof-to-code view.
nodes.claim_ceiling: The tour can explain the graph but cannot prove that a person understood it.

nodes.label: Read the four areas from left to right
nodes.plain_language: Business meaning says what matters. DomainSpec formalizes it. The proof and architecture bridge records obligations, candidate shapes, and gaps. System evidence shows the code and tests that actually exist.

integration_sentences.sentence: Business meaning supplies the promise; DomainSpec turns that promise into stable typed concepts and clauses without taking ownership of it.
DomainSpec's typed clauses and derivation model feed the bridge, where obligations, candidate code shapes, and unresolved gaps stay explicit.
The bridge tells us which code and tests to inspect, while system evidence reports only what currently exists and executes.

nodes.claim_ceiling: Explains lane roles without changing the meaning or state of any node.

nodes.label: See how the boxes integrate in pairs
nodes.plain_language: Follow three real relationships: business meaning becomes a DomainSpec classification, an Obligation gets a generated test representation, and the use case depends on the decision function. Each relationship has a different evidentiary strength.

integration_sentences.sentence: GenerateSettlement integrates with DomainSpec through classification: the business action becomes an Operation while its meaning remains owned by the business concept.
FS-POST-001 integrates with test generation through a named test case, but that test is skipped, so the connection records coverage intent rather than proof.
The settlement use case integrates with the decision function by calling it before effects; this is system control flow, not a DomainSpec identity.

nodes.claim_ceiling: Explains three supported integrations without treating classification, representation, or dependency as proof identity.

nodes.label: Follow only the path the evidence supports
nodes.plain_language: GenerateSettlement is classified as a DomainSpec Operation. That type candidate-maps to an Operation implementation shape, which shapes a candidate code contract. The path stops there: it does not identify or generate the handwritten function.

integration_sentences.sentence: The business action connects to DS-D1.4 through classification, telling the architecture layer that the required realization must behave as a state-changing Operation.
The DomainSpec Operation connects to an Operation implementation shape through a candidate mapping, which narrows the software form without selecting code.
The architecture shape connects to the settlement code contract by defining the inputs and ordered effects that a future bound implementation must support.

nodes.claim_ceiling: Explains a candidate architecture path; it does not bind or generate code.

nodes.label: Understand why the missing-link box matters
nodes.plain_language: P4 and FS-POST-001 both acknowledge the same missing origin evidence. There is deliberately no direct P4-to-Obligation edge until DomainSpec emits an ontology-native subject reference.

integration_sentences.sentence: P4 connects to the origin-gap node to state that its derived Obligation identity has not yet been established.
FS-POST-001 connects to the same origin-gap node because it lacks a graph digest, node ID, clause ID, and JSON pointer back to P4.
P4 and FS-POST-001 do not integrate directly today; both point to the shared gap until DomainSpec emits an ontology-native subject reference.

nodes.claim_ceiling: Makes the missing identity visible; it does not infer that identity.
